keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the founding year, which Cliopatria lacks (its first shape is 886). 'Established by Ashot I of the Bagratuni dynasty in the early 880s'; infobox rulers Ashot I (885-890), capital Bagaran (885-890). [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: the keyframe was an 80 km radius around Ani (about 20,000 km2), a factor 5 below the 886 shape (99,224 km2) with no event between the two. The page has the Caliph recognising Ashot 'as prince of princes in 862 and, later on, as king (in 884 or 885)' and his authority carried over 'Georgia, Caucasian Albania', so the 886 shape is applied to 885 and the founding event carries it; nothing on the page supports a fivefold expansion in one year.]

Cliopatria's 99,224 km2 (bbox 41.6-47.1E, 37.6-41.3N) takes in Ayrarat, Shirak, Vaspurakan and Syunik (gazetteer test 2026-10-31: 14 cells of Syunik, none of the Nakhchivan region, none of Ardahan or Artvin). The infobox gives no area; the body says Ashot's authority 'extended over Georgia, Caucasian Albania, and several Arab emirates', so the shape is a mixture of direct land and overlordship (Syunik was a Bagratid vassal, Dvin an Arab stronghold until 892). Accepted at the precision of the era; soft.

97,862 km2 (-1.4 percent), the year Smbat I's rule was 'firmly established' and he 'captured Dvin, the last Arab stronghold in Armenia' (21 April 892 on the Bagratid page). The shape's east edge shrinks from 47.1E to 46.9E; the pages say nothing of land lost, so noise.

correction.text: the 898 shape plus Nakhchivan, valid for 898-901 only; Smbat I granted Nakhchavan to Ashot Artsruni in 902

keyframe_review.note: 98,064 km2, plus Nakhchivan (about 5,300 km2; no Cliopatria shape of 886-1027 contains a cell of it, gazetteer test 2026-10-31), for 898-901: in 902 'King Smbat I granted Nakhchavan to his maternal cousin Ashot Artsruni', so it was Bagratid until then. From 902 the keyframes _902 to _909 follow the ledger: Nakhchivan to Vaspurakan 902 and back 904 (after Ashot's death 'the Armenian king took Nakhichevan away from Vaspurakan'), Ardahan annexed 903 (to 911), Vaspurakan leaves in 908 ('Gagik turned to Yusuf, who sent him a crown in 908 and recognized him as the King of All Armenians'), Nakhchivan lost to Yusuf in 909. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: was 'unchanged shape, valid for 898-907 only'.] [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 898..907 from this entry's own 'valid for 898-907 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

Ardahan also lies inside every Cliopatria Kingdom of the Iberians shape (20 of 20 cells), so the two shapes overlap here until 910; Klarjeti (Artvin) is not added, see the 903 ledger event.

correction.text: the 898 shape plus Ardahan and Nakhchivan, taken back from Vaspurakan in 904

keyframe_review.note: 904-907: the 898 shape plus Ardahan and Nakhchivan ('after Ashot's death in 904, the Armenian king took Nakhichevan away from Vaspurakan').

correction.text: Bagratid Armenia without Vaspurakan (the 911 shape) plus Ardahan and Nakhchivan, from the Artsruni crown of 908

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 908: Cliopatria's 911 shape (56,711 km2, without Vaspurakan, the lands south of 38.9N) applied three years earlier, from Gagik Artsruni's crown of 908 ('Some sources give different dates for Gagik's crown (908 vs. 909)'), plus Ardahan and Nakhchivan (the page has Nakhichevan 'most likely granted by the Armenian king to Syunik in 908', a Bagratid vassal). [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: was 908-910 without Ardahan or Nakhchivan; 909-910 are now keyframe _909.]

correction.text: the 911 shape plus Ardahan; Nakhchivan lost to Yusuf in 909

keyframe_review.note: 909-910: the 911 shape plus Ardahan. 'In 909 Yusuf took Nakhichevan and, together with Gagik, gained control of Siunikh' (Yusuf page); Smbat was beaten at Dzknavachar in 910, when 'Arab emirs who had paid tribute to Smbat revolted' (Smbat I page). Ardahan goes in 911 (bridged), when Cliopatria's 911 shape begins.

56,711 km2: the Armenia of Ayrarat and Shirak without Vaspurakan. Smbat surrendered to Yusuf in 914 and was beheaded; the page has no other land change for 911-935 (civil war 918-920, Yusuf released 923, died 929, Byzantine army at Dvin 928). From 911 the shape contains none of Ardahan (ledger: end of the 903 annexation, bridged to 911).
58,941 km2 (+3.9 percent); the page has nothing for 936 (Abas I, 928-953) and records only an 'invasion by king Ber of Abkhazia in 943'; noise or an unrecorded gain, confidence low.

58,869 km2, stable to 999 in Cliopatria, kept to 1000 here. Within it the page dates: Ani capital 961, Dzoraget given to Gurgen in 966, Tashir to Kiurike with the royal title in 979 (Tashir-Dzoraget page), Syunik independent 987 and again under overlordship 988 (Syunik page). Inside it lies Kars (37 of the 41 cells of Kars province), where the page has Ashot III's brother Mushegh I ruling as king from 963 (ledger: vassal_start kingdom-of-kars 963), so the sub-kingdom is a lighter tint on land the shape already holds.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 947-1000 (one year longer than Cliopatria's 999: the Byzantine gain in the west is dated 1001)

keyframe_review.note: 53,011 km2 (-9.9 percent), applied from 1001: the west edge moves from 41.6E to 42.8E, the strip toward Tayk and Tao, which reaches Phasiane (Pasinler, 41.68E) at its western end. Basil II page: 'In 1001, after the death of David of Tao, Basil inherited Tao, Phasiane and Speri' (the theme of Iberia at Theodosiopolis), the date the byzantine-empire dossier also has (1001, from David III); Cliopatria draws the cut in 1000. The Gagik I page is silent on the loss; 'from Shamkor to Vagharshakert, and from the Kura River to Apahunik near Lake Van' is its extent and names Vayots Dzor, Khachen, Nakhichevan and Dvin as Gagik's gains. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: was dated 1000 at confidence 1.]

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid from 1001 (1001-1009); 1000 keeps the 947 shape

keyframe_review.note: 52,795 km2, unchanged in extent. The page has the Church of St Gregory at Ani (1001-10) and Gagik's reign to 1017/1020, no land change in 1010. Valid to 1020 only: Gagik I died in 1017 or 1020 and Ashot IV's division follows (keyframes _1021 to _1028).

correction.text: the 1028 shape applied from 1021: Hovhannes-Smbat keeps Ani and 'limited areas around the capital', Ashot IV rules 'further Armenian provinces closer to Persia and Georgia'

keyframe_review.note: 1021 only: 38,971 km2. 'Rebelled in 1021 ... After a compromise, Hovhannes-Smbat kept power on limited areas around the capital' and Ashot became a concurrent king (Hovhannes-Smbat III page); Cliopatria draws the cut in 1028, so the shape is applied seven years earlier on the page's date. Dvin is still inside.

correction.text: the 1028 shape without Dvin, which Fadl I took from the Bagratids in 1022

keyframe_review.note: 1022-1027: the 1028 shape without Dvin (8 cells, about 2,000 km2): 'He took Dvin from Armenian Bagratids in 1022' (Shaddadids page).

38,971 km2 (-26.2 percent): the south and east are cut (bbox 42.8-46.0E, 39.2-41.3N against 46.9E, 38.9N before); the shape holds none of Syunik, Vayots Dzor or the Nakhchivan region (gazetteer test 2026-10-31). Cliopatria draws the cut in 1028; the pages date its likelier cause to 1021, when Ashot IV rebelled and, after a compromise, ruled the 'further Armenian provinces closer to Persia and Georgia' as a concurrent king while Hovhannes-Smbat kept 'limited areas around the capital' (Hovhannes-Smbat III page; the Gagik I page: 'his younger son Ashot broke away'). Keyframes _1021 and _1022 apply the shape from 1021; Dvin is cut from 1022 (Shaddadids page). [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: the cut was read as a loss to Syunik at confidence 1, which no page supports (the Syunik page is silent on 1020-1045); the 1028 date is Cliopatria's.]

correction.text: the 1028 shape without Dvin (taken by the Shaddadids in 1022), valid for 1028-1033

keyframe_review.note: 39,164 km2 (+0.5 percent): noise; the page has the brothers Hovhannes-Smbat and Ashot IV reigning to 1040-41. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: Dvin, taken by the Shaddadids in 1022, is cut from this shape.]

Same extent as 1034 to 1045: Gagik II 'reigned only for a period of two years', 'In 1044, the Byzantines twice invaded Ani but failed to conquer it', and in 1045 the Catholicos 'surrendered Ani to the Byzantines'. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: Dvin, taken by the Shaddadids in 1022, is cut from this shape.]

region.text: the kingdom of Ashot I as Cliopatria draws it from 886: Ayrarat and Shirak around Bagaran and Ani, with Vaspurakan and Syunik under its overlordship

ledger.note: 885: Ashot I is crowned king of Armenia. 'The Caliph ... recognized Ashot as prince of princes in 862 and, later on, as king (in 884 or 885)'; 'In 884, the Caliph Al-Mu'tamid sent a crown to Ashot'; he 'chose to conclude an alliance with the Byzantines in 885'; Bagaran is the first capital. The page gives the founding as 'the early 880s' and the crowning as 884 or 885; 885 is the infobox's first reign year. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: the region was an 80 km radius around Ani (about 20,000 km2) while Cliopatria's 886 shape is 99,224 km2 with no event between; the page has the Caliph recognising Ashot as prince of princes in 862 and as king in 884 or 885, with authority over 'Georgia, Caucasian Albania', so the founding event carries the 886 shape (abbasid-caliphate's 886 loss is its mirror).]

Late 9th century: Syunik under the Bagratid kings. 'Vasak Ishkhanik took the royal title while continuing to recognize the overlordship of the Bagratid kings of Armenia'; the page gives no year ('Late 9th c. to 987: vassal, with royal title'), so 885 is the start of the Bagratid kingship. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: the Syunik page dates the entry to 885: 'in 885, Syunik became part of the administrative territory of the emirate'. I read the emirate as the Armenian realm that Ashot I headed (prince of princes from 862, king from 884/885); the page does not name him, so the year is the page's and the reading mine (confidence 1 to 2).]
890: the capital moves from Bagaran to Shirakavan (infobox: Bagaran 885-890, Shirakavan 890-929).

region.text: Dvin, 'the last Arab stronghold in Armenia'

ledger.note: April 892: Smbat I retakes Dvin. 'On April 21, 892, he recaptured the historic city of Dvin from the Arabs'; he was 'crowned king in 892' and the Caliph al-Mu'tadid sent a crown (Smbat I page). The Arabs retook it in 901 (Yusuf) and Smbat recovered it. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: no 901 loss and recovery pair is recorded. Smbat I page: 'In 901, Afshin was succeeded by Yusuf, who invaded Armenia and captured Dvin' and 'Smbat besieged the city and recaptured it'; the sentence dates Yusuf's succession, not the capture, the recovery has no year, the Yusuf ibn Abi'l-Saj and Sajid dynasty pages do not mention the capture, and the sajid-dynasty dossier has no 901 Dvin event, so a pair would net to zero within a year or two and lack a mirror. Later history of Dvin: see the 1022 loss.]
902: Smbat I grants Nakhchavan to Ashot Artsruni. 'In 902, King Smbat I granted Nakhchavan to his maternal cousin Ashot Artsruni'; it passes to Vaspurakan.

region.text: Abkhazian districts, including Klarjeti and Ardahan

ledger.note: 903: Smbat I annexes Abkhazian districts. 'In 903, the Abkhazians began raiding Gugark and Iberia. Smbat then annexed Abkhazian districts, including Klarjeti and Ardahan.' The year is the raid's; the page gives none for the annexation and does not say the districts were lost or retaken. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: the event drew Ardahan and Artvin (Klarjeti). Artvin is the found region and core of kingdom-of-the-iberians (Cliopatria's 814-999 shapes hold all 32 Artvin cells and all 20 Ardahan cells), and that dossier records no 903 loss, so only Ardahan is kept, with an end in 911 and keyframes _903 to _909. Klarjeti stays with the Iberians in the drawing: the Kingdom of the Iberians page has Adarnase 'dispossessed by Constantine III in 904' and no Bagratid hold, and the two pages are not reconciled. Ardahan still overlaps the Iberians' shape 903-910; kingdom-of-the-iberians (verdict thin, not reopened) would need a mirror loss and return.]

904: Smbat I takes Nakhchavan back. 'After the death of Sargis-Ashot in 904, the rule of Vaspurakan passed to his middle brother, Gagik'; the page has Smbat take Nakhchavan from Vaspurakan after Ashot Artsruni's death and later place it under the Siunis (the Syunik page has 902 or 903 for the cession). The recovery's year is the page's 904 for the death.

908: Vaspurakan leaves under its own king. Gagik Artsruni 'turned to Yusuf, who sent him a crown in 908 and recognized him as the King of All Armenians'; some sources have 909, Cliopatria draws the separate Vaspurakan from 911. Nakhchavan 'was most likely granted by the Armenian king to Syunik in 908', i.e. to a Bagratid vassal.

region.text: Syunik and the Ararat plain toward Dvin

ledger.note: 909: Yusuf of Azerbaijan invades Armenia. 'In 909, Yusuf gathered a large army and launched a campaign against Armenia'; he entered Syunik and moved toward Dvin; Smbat paid 60,000 gold coins and was pursued to Tayk; the decisive battle was at Dzknavachar in 910.

909: Yusuf takes Nakhichevan. 'In 909 Yusuf took Nakhichevan and, together with Gagik, gained control of Siunikh' (Yusuf ibn Abi'l-Saj page; the mirror of sajid-dynasty /ledger/2); the page speaks of a 'dispute with the Bagratid over the province of Nakhichevan', and the Smbat I page has the city 'most likely granted by the Armenian king to Syunik in 908'. Syunik itself is not recorded as lost: the Yusuf page has Yusuf gaining Siunikh 'together with Gagik', the Smbat I page only that Yusuf 'moved northward and entered Syunik' and was joined at the border by Gagik Artsruni, and the Syunik page is silent on 909-914; Cliopatria's 911-1027 shapes keep Syunik, so it stays a Bagratid vassal and its 909-914 status is the contest below. The Gagik I page says Gagik I later united Nakhichevan (no year, 989-1020): not recorded as a gain for lack of a date.

region.text: Ardahan, annexed from the Abkhazians in 903

ledger.note: c. 911: the Ardahan annexation lapses. No page gives an end: the Smbat I page does not say the Abkhazian districts were lost or retaken. Smbat was beaten at Dzknavachar in 910 and surrendered in 914, and Cliopatria's 911 shape (56,711 km2) contains none of Ardahan, so the end is bridged to 911. Bridging.

region.text: Syunik and the Ararat plain toward Dvin

ledger.note: 914: Smbat I surrenders and is killed. 'Smbat finally decided to surrender himself to Yusuf in 914'; 'Yusuf had Smbat beheaded, and his body was crucified on the gates of Dvin'. Yusuf stays a threat until his death in 929 (Bagratid Armenia page: Kourkouas at Dvin in 928); the page records no treaty, so 914 is the end of the war with Smbat.
929: the capital moves from Shirakavan to Kars (infobox: Kars 929-961).
961: Ashot III relocates the capital from Kars to Ani, the year of his investiture as king.

963: Mushegh I founds the Kingdom of Kars (Vanand) as a Bagratid sub-kingdom. Kingdom of Kars page: 'formed in the year 963 by the son of Abas I of Armenia, Mushegh Bagratuni (d. 984)', capital Kars; 'the extent of its actual independence from the Kingdom of Ani is uncertain' and 'it was always in the possession of the relatives of the rulers of Ani'. The Bagratid Armenia page: Ashot III 'had sent his brother Mushegh I to rule in Kars (Vanand) and had allowed him to use the title of king' (no year). The year is the Kars page's; reading the kingdom as a vassal is mine.

979: Tashir is granted to Kiurike as a vassal kingdom. 'In 979 King Smbat II of Armenia granted the province of Tashir to his brother Kiurike with the title of king'; infobox 'Vassal of: Bagratid Armenia'. The Bagratid page has Dzoraget given to Gurgen in 966. Tashir is read as the Lori province; Kiurike's revolt of 1001 failed.
987: Syunik declares itself a separate kingdom. 'It was only in 987, when the central authority of the Bagratids had weakened' that Smbat I of Syunik made it independent.

988: Syunik again recognises the Bagratid king. After Abu'l-Hayja died, Smbat I of Syunik 'recognized Smbat II of Armenia's overlordship' (paraphrase of the page's 988 entry). [Confidence lowered from 3 to 2, reviewer eu-19-c, 2026-10-31: the page dates Abu'l-Hayja's death to 988 and puts the recognition 'After the death of Abu al-Haij' with no year of its own.]

region.text: Vayots Dzor, Chahuk and part of Tsghukk

ledger.note: 989-1020: Gagik I takes Vayots Dzor from Syunik. 'Gagik I (r. 989-1020), took the territories of Vayots Dzor, Chahuk, and part of Tsghukk from Syunik'; the Gagik I page adds Khachen, Nakhichevan and Dvin as his gains. The page dates only the reign, so 989 (its start) is bridging. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: reopened: the Syunik page says 'King Gagik I (989-1020) took some regions (Jahuk and part of the Pot), including Vayots Dzor, from his vassal'; the Gagik I page lists 'Vayots Dzor, Khachen, Nakhichevan and the city of Dvin' as united under him; neither gives a year, so 989 stays the reign's start (confidence 1). Cliopatria's 947 shape already holds all of Vayots Dzor (8 cells), so the shape shows no gain in 989.]

region.text: the strip of the 999 shape that is not in the 1000 shape, toward Tayk and Phasiane

ledger.note: 1001: the western strip toward Tayk goes to Byzantium. Basil II page: 'In 1001, after the death of David of Tao, Basil inherited Tao, Phasiane and Speri', organised into the theme of Iberia at Theodosiopolis. The strip Cliopatria cuts in 1000 (west edge 41.6E to 42.8E) reaches Phasiane (Pasinler, 41.68E), so the redraw is read as this inheritance and dated 1001 (the Iberians dossier has 1000/1001). byzantine-empire /ledger/83 records the 1001 gain from David III of Tao, not from the Bagratids: whether the strip was Bagratid land or David's is not settled by the pages (the Gagik I page is silent). The year is the page's, the region my reading of the redraw. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: was dated 1000 at confidence 1.]

region.text: the lands of the 1027 shape that are not in the 1028 shape, toward Syunik, Vayots Dzor and the east: the 'further Armenian provinces closer to Persia and Georgia'

ledger.note: 1021: the kingdom divides between the brothers Hovhannes-Smbat III and Ashot IV. Hovhannes-Smbat III page: Ashot 'rebelled in 1021', and after a compromise Hovhannes-Smbat kept power 'on limited areas around the capital' while Ashot became a concurrent king ruling 'further Armenian provinces closer to Persia and Georgia'; the Gagik I page: Ashot 'broke away and proclaimed independence in the Kingdom of Lori-Dzoraget'; the Bagratid Armenia page: 'the kingdom was split between his two sons'. Cliopatria draws the cut in 1028 (-26 percent; the shape holds no Syunik, Vayots Dzor or Nakhchivan). The year is the page's (the compromise itself is undated); the region is the Cliopatria difference, my reading of 'closer to Persia'. Ashot IV is a Bagratid co-king, so the rendering agent may prefer a lighter tint of this state's colour for his share; no separate dossier is implied. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: this replaces the 1028 loss to kingdom-of-syunik at confidence 1, which no page supports.]

1022: Fadl I takes Dvin. Shaddadids page: 'He took Dvin from Armenian Bagratids in 1022' (the mirror of shaddadids /ledger/3). The pages disagree about Dvin before that: the Smbat I page has Smbat's body crucified at its gates in 914 and the Yusuf page has Yusuf setting up the rival king Sparapet Ashot there; the Bagratid Armenia page has the anti-king Ashot holding it in 918-920, 'the Arabs and Ashot' defending it in 928, Ashot III failing to take it 'from the Shaddadid emir' in 953, and Ashot IV unable to occupy it after Gagik I 'because of its capture by the Shaddadid'; the Gagik I and Syunik pages have Gagik I uniting or seizing it (no year). Cliopatria draws Dvin inside every Bagratid shape 886-1045, so it is kept until 1022; whether it was continuously Bagratid in 914-1022 is not settled. Keyframes _1022 to _1040 cut it.

1045: Kiurike II becomes independent of the fallen Bagratids. 'After the fall of the Bagratid Kingdom of Armenia in 1045, Kiurike II was bestowed by the Byzantines' the title of Kouropalates and became independent.

1045: the Bagratid overlordship of Syunik ends with the kingdom. The Syunik page gives no end of the relation; its king Smbat II helped David I Anhoghin against the Shaddadids in 1040 and Grigor I reigned 1044-1084. [Revised 2026-10-31, eu-19-c repair: reopened the Syunik page: it states neither Syunik's status in 1045 nor an end to the Bagratid overlordship, and Cliopatria's shapes hold no Syunik after 1021/1028; the vassal tint is kept to 1045 as the last year of the Bagratid kingship (confidence 1).]

1045: with Ani surrendered, Kars no longer answers to a Bagratid king of Ani. Kingdom of Kars page: 'after Ani's capture by the Byzantine Empire in 1045, the Bagratuni title "King of Kings" held by the ruler of Ani was transferred to the ruler of Kars'; the kingdom itself lasts until Gagik-Abas ceded it to Byzantium in 1065 (text; infobox 1064).

region.text: Ani and the remaining Bagratid lands

ledger.note: 1045: Ani passes to Byzantium. 'Catholicos Petros Getadardz ... surrendered Ani to the Byzantines in 1045'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1045'; Hovhannes-Smbat had pledged in 1022 that the kingdom would pass to the Byzantines after his death, the brothers died in 1040-41 and 'the Byzantines twice invaded Ani' in 1044. Gagik-Abas kept a rump at Kars until the Turks took it in 1065.

wars.name: Sajid campaigns against Armenia

zones.text: Syunik and the Ararat plain toward Dvin

wars.outcome: Yusuf captured Dvin in 901 (retaken by Smbat), crowned Gagik Artsruni in 908, invaded in 909, beat Smbat at Dzknavachar in 910 and had him beheaded in 914; Vaspurakan leaves the kingdom.
wars.note: The Bagratid page adds that Yusuf instigated a failed rebellion against the Caliph in 919, was released in 923, and died in 929; civil war raged 918-920. The Yusuf ibn Abi'l-Saj page adds 'In 909 Yusuf took Nakhichevan and, together with Gagik, gained control of Siunikh' (ledger 909), and has Smbat executed 'before the fortress' walls' after his capture around 913.

wars.name: Abkhazian invasion of 943
wars.outcome: An 'invasion by king Ber of Abkhazia in 943'; no land change is recorded.

wars.name: Battle of Tsumb
wars.outcome: 'whose armies defeated Mamlan, the emir of Khorasan, in 998 in the village of Tsumb, northeast of Lake Van': the sentence follows Gagik I's alliance with Bagrat III and Gurgen of Iberia, whose armies are meant.
wars.note: The battle's article title was not checked; the Gagik I page links the alliance with Bagrat III and Gurgen of Iberia.

wars.name: Byzantine invasions of Ani
wars.outcome: 'In 1044, the Byzantines twice invaded Ani but failed to conquer it'; in 1045 Catholicos Petros Getadardz surrendered Ani to the Byzantines.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary or area for any year; the kingdom was a loose overlordship of princes (Syunik, Tashir-Dzoraget, Vaspurakan) and the shape mixes direct land and suzerainty.

notes:
BUDGET. Five pages for 11 shapes (the budget), six more opened in the 2026-10-31 repair (Yusuf, Sajid, Shaddadids, Kars, Hovhannes-Smbat III, Basil II). Not opened: the Vaspurakan page, Seshat. The 1010 shape rests on silence; the 1001 and 1021 events now rest on pages, the 1028 date on Cliopatria.

START. 885 (infobox: Ashot I 885-890, Bagaran 885-890; the Caliph's crown 884 or 885), against Cliopatria's 886 and the page's 'early 880s'. The 885 keyframe is a core around Ani, which is a reading.

OVERLAP WITH THE IBERIANS. The 903 gain of 'Klarjeti and Ardahan' from the Abkhazians (Smbat I page) lies inside Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Iberians shape (814-999); after the repair only Ardahan is drawn (903-910), Artvin (Klarjeti) is left to the Iberians, and the Iberians dossier needs a mirror loss. The Kingdom of the Iberians page has Adarnase 'dispossessed by Constantine III in 904' and crowned by Smbat in 899. The pages do not reconcile; a gap-filler should open the Armenian-Georgian frontier sources.

VASSALS. This dossier carries the Bagratid side of Syunik (885-987, 988-1045) and Tashir-Dzoraget (979-1045). Not recorded: Taron (Byzantines 'regarded the Bagratuni princes of Taron as vassals'; 'Taron ... annexed ... in 966'), Vaspurakan after 908, Kars is now a vassal 963-1045 (Kars page); its rump to 1065 is not drawn here, the Arab emirates and Georgian princes in Ashot's 'authority'. kingdom-of-syunik, kingdom-of-tashir-dzoraget and kingdom-of-artsakh need dossiers (eu-19-x); Kingdom of Kars (to 1065) too.

CAPITALS. Bagaran and Shirakavan coordinates are approximate (neither is in the gazetteer). Dvin is not in the gazetteer either: Artashat (about 10 km away) stands in for it.

CONFLICTS. Infobox Ani 961-1045 against body Kars to 961; Gagik I's death 1017 or 1020; the brothers' deaths 1040-41; Smbat I's coronation 892 (Bagratid page) against a caliphal crown 892 (Smbat I page). Pages disagree on who ceded Nakhchavan in 902/903 (Smbat I against Smbat II on the Syunik page).

AREA. The infobox gives none; the 99,224 km2 of 886 is the largest shape and includes Vaspurakan and Syunik, which the page treats as vassals or independent princes.

REPAIR 2026-10-31 (eu-19-c). 886: found region is the 886 shape. 903: Artvin dropped, Ardahan to 911. 909: Nakhchivan lost to the Sajids (Yusuf page). 963-1045: Kars vassal. 1001: western strip dated by the Basil II page. 1021: division with Ashot IV replaces the 1028 loss to Syunik. 1022: Dvin lost to the Shaddadids. 901 Dvin: no pair, reasons in the 892 event. Open: who held Dvin 914-1022 (pages conflict), Gagik I's undated union of Nakhichevan, Khachen and Dvin, the date of the Ashot IV compromise, and the Syunik status after 1021.
